title: Best Infographic Designers (2026): How to Hire One
description: How to hire an infographic designer: what the package should include, how to prepare your data, what drives the price and red flags.
intro: An infographic turns numbers, steps or comparisons into a picture people understand at a glance. Good ones are shared, saved and linked to. Bad ones look busy, misrepresent data or cannot be read on a phone. Most problems start with unclear content: the designer can only make your information clear if you know what it is saying. This guide helps you prepare and order well.

faq.q: Do I need to supply the content?
faq.a: Usually yes. Most designers visualize content you provide: the facts, numbers, sources and the main message. Some offer research or writing as an extra.

faq.q: Which format should the infographic be?
faq.a: Tall images suit blogs and Pinterest, square or 4:5 suits social feeds, and print needs a high-resolution PDF. Ask for every format you will use.

faq.q: How do I make sure the data is shown honestly?
faq.a: Ask for charts that start at zero where appropriate, consistent scales and clear labels. Always include sources. A misleading chart damages trust even if it was accidental.

faq.q: Can I get an editable file?
faq.a: Ask for the source file so you can update numbers later without starting over.
Yes. Use readable text sizes and good contrast, and publish the key facts as text alongside the image for screen readers and search engines.
